description: Widely used mantras with meaning, and notes on when and how they are traditionally chanted.

items.text:
ॐ भूर्भुवः स्वः।
तत्सवितुर्वरेण्यं।
भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि।
धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात्॥
items.transliteration:
om bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ
tat savitur vareṇyaṁ
bhargo devasya dhīmahi
dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt

translations.en: Om. We meditate on the radiant splendour of the Sun, the most worthy of reverence, across the three worlds. May it awaken our understanding.
translations.hi: ॐ। हम तीनों लोकों में व्याप्त, सबसे पूजनीय सविता (सूर्य) के दिव्य तेज का ध्यान करते हैं। वह हमारी बुद्धि को प्रेरित करे।

items.summary_1line: The mother of the Vedic mantras
items.summary_2to3line: A prayer to the sun for illumination of the mind — not for things, but for clear understanding.
items.bodh_3to4line: Traditionally chanted at the three twilight junctions (dawn, noon, dusk), 3, 9, 27 or 108 times. It is the core of sandhya vandana. Anyone may chant it; the counts are a discipline, not a requirement.

items.text:
ॐ त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे सुगन्धिं पुष्टिवर्धनम्।
उर्वारुकमिव बन्धनान् मृत्योर्मुक्षीय मामृतात्॥
items.transliteration:
om tryambakaṁ yajāmahe sugandhiṁ puṣṭi-vardhanam
urvārukam iva bandhanān mṛtyor mukṣīya māmṛtāt

translations.en: Om. We worship the three-eyed one, fragrant, who nourishes all beings. May he release us from death as a cucumber is freed from its vine — and not from immortality.
translations.hi: ॐ। हम त्रिनेत्रधारी, सुगंधित, पुष्टि बढ़ाने वाले शिव की उपासना करते हैं। जैसे खीरा बेल से अलग होता है, वैसे ही वे हमें मृत्यु के बंधन से मुक्त करें — अमरता से नहीं।

items.summary_2to3line: It asks for release from what binds us — illness, fear, the grip of mortality — while asking to be kept in life, not taken from it.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted in times of illness, before a medical procedure, on birthdays and on Shivratri, often 108 times. Many families chant it as a daily protective mantra.

translations.en: Om, I bow to Shiva — to the auspicious one within.
translations.hi: ॐ, मैं शिव को नमन करता हूँ — भीतर स्थित कल्याणकारी को।

items.summary_2to3line: The five syllables are said to stand for the five elements; the mantra is a bow to the auspicious presence in all of them.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted silently or aloud at any time, commonly 108 times on a mala. It needs no special setting — many people repeat it while walking or working.

items.text:
वक्रतुण्ड महाकाय सूर्यकोटि समप्रभ।
निर्विघ्नं कुरु मे देव सर्वकार्येषु सर्वदा॥
items.transliteration:
vakratuṇḍa mahākāya sūrya-koṭi sama-prabha
nirvighnaṁ kuru me deva sarva-kāryeṣu sarvadā

translations.en: O curved-trunked one, of great body, radiant as a million suns — remove my obstacles, O Lord, in all my undertakings, always.
translations.hi: हे वक्रतुंड, महाकाय, करोड़ों सूर्यों के समान तेजस्वी! हे देव, मेरे सभी कार्यों में सदा विघ्न दूर कीजिए।

items.summary_2to3line: A single request, made to Ganesha, for the road ahead to be clear.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted once at the start of a journey, an exam, a new job, a puja — any beginning. Ganesha is invoked first by convention.

items.text:
हरे कृष्ण हरे कृष्ण कृष्ण कृष्ण हरे हरे।
हरे राम हरे राम राम राम हरे हरे॥
items.transliteration:
hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare

translations.en: Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna, Hare Hare; Hare Rama, Hare Rama, Rama Rama, Hare Hare.
translations.hi: हरे कृष्ण हरे कृष्ण, कृष्ण कृष्ण हरे हरे। हरे राम हरे राम, राम राम हरे हरे।

items.summary_1line: The great mantra of the names
items.summary_2to3line: Sixteen names of the divine in a call-and-response form; it is sung rather than recited, and needs no meaning to be worked with.
items.bodh_3to4line: Sung in kirtan, alone or in a group, with or without a count. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition it is the principal practice of the age.

translations.en: Om. I bow to the Lord Vasudeva (Krishna).
translations.hi: ॐ। मैं भगवान वासुदेव (कृष्ण) को नमन करता हूँ।

items.summary_2to3line: A bow to Vasudeva, the divine who dwells in all things. It is a complete prayer in four words.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted 108 times on a mala, commonly on Ekadashi, Vaikuntha Ekadashi and Krishna Janmashtami, and as a daily remembrance.

translations.en: Om, I bow to Saraswati, with the seed syllable Aim.
translations.hi: ॐ, ऐं बीज सहित मैं सरस्वती को नमन करता हूँ।

items.summary_2to3line: A single-line invocation of Saraswati, used to ask for clarity of speech, memory and study.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted before study, before an examination, or on Vasant Panchami — often 108 times, or simply three times before opening a book.

items.text: ॐ श्रीं ह्रीं श्रीं कमले कमलालये प्रसीद प्रसीद॥
items.transliteration: om śrīṁ hrīṁ śrīṁ kamale kamalālaye prasīda prasīda

translations.en: Om, Shrim Hrim Shrim — O you who dwell in the lotus, be pleased, be pleased.
translations.hi: ॐ, श्रीं ह्रीं श्रीं — हे कमल में निवास करने वाली, प्रसन्न होइए, प्रसन्न होइए।

items.summary_2to3line: It calls on the goddess who sits in the lotus, asking her to turn her attention toward the household.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted on Fridays, on Diwali, and during Lakshmi puja, commonly 108 times. Often done after cleaning the house and lighting a lamp.

items.text: ॐ ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं चामुण्डायै विच्चे॥
items.transliteration: om aiṁ hrīṁ klīṁ cāmuṇḍāyai vicce

translations.en: Om, Aim Hrim Klim — to Chamunda, the one who discerns.
translations.hi: ॐ, ऐं ह्रीं क्लीं — विवेक रखने वाली चामुंडा को नमन।

items.summary_1line: A bija mantra of the Mother goddess
items.summary_2to3line: Three seed syllables followed by an address to the fierce form of the goddess, invoked for courage and protection.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted during Navratri and on Durga puja days, often 108 times. Traditionally recited with a steady, unhurried breath.

items.text: ॐ हं हनुमते रुद्रात्मकाय हुं फट्॥
items.transliteration: om haṁ hanumate rudrātmakāya huṁ phaṭ

translations.en: Om, Ham — to Hanuman, who is of the nature of Rudra, Hum Phat.
translations.hi: ॐ, हं — रुद्र स्वरूप हनुमान को नमन, हुं फट्।

items.summary_2to3line: It invokes Hanuman as Rudra's own form — strength in service — and is used when courage is needed.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted on Tuesdays and Saturdays, often 108 times, or a single round before something difficult.

items.text:
ॐ असतो मा सद्गमय।
तमसो मा ज्योतिर्गमय।
मृत्योर्मा अमृतं गमय।
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः॥
items.transliteration:
om asato mā sad gamaya
tamaso mā jyotir gamaya
mṛtyor mā amṛtaṁ gamaya
om śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ

translations.en: Lead me from the unreal to the real; from darkness to light; from death to immortality. Om, peace, peace, peace.
translations.hi: हे प्रभु, मुझे असत्य से सत्य की ओर, अंधकार से प्रकाश की ओर, मृत्यु से अमरता की ओर ले चलिए। ॐ, शांति, शांति, शांति।

items.summary_1line: A prayer for three kinds of light
items.summary_2to3line: Three paired requests — real over unreal, light over dark, life over death — followed by peace invoked three times.
items.bodh_3to4line: Chanted at the end of a reading, a havan or a puja, and often at the start of study. The triple shanti is a standard closing.
